title: SPARQL builtins STRLEN/ENCODE_FOR_URI/LANGMATCHES wrongly STR()-coerced non-string operands (FIXED)
description:
Found + FIXED during sq-6qkq (per-builtin error-path table test), branch test-builtin-errors.

DIVERGENCE (SPARQL 1.1 type-error rule): three string builtins used the lax value_str() coercion (which stringifies IRIs/numbers/booleans like STR()) where the spec requires a STRING LITERAL operand, so a type-error input wrongly produced a VALUE instead of an expression error:
  - STRLEN(<iri>)        returned the IRI's char count (e.g. 11) instead of error  [exec.rs F::StrLen, SPARQL 1.1 §17.4.3.2 — xsd:integer STRLEN(string literal)]
  - ENCODE_FOR_URI(123)  returned simple literal "123" instead of error           [exec.rs F::EncodeForUri, §17.4.3.12 — simple literal ENCODE_FOR_URI(string literal)]
  - LANGMATCHES(123,'en') returned false (a value) instead of error                 [exec.rs F::LangMatches, §17.4.3.15 — xsd:boolean langMatches(simple literal, simple literal)]

FIX: switched those three arms from value_str() to str_lit() (accepts simple/lang-tagged/xsd:string, rejects IRI/number/boolean -> Value::Error). Tagged [OPUS-4.8] in exec.rs. All 144 existing engine lib tests still pass; new builtin_error_paths table test (44 builtins x {valid,type-error,(boundary)}) is green. clippy -D warnings clean. W3C conformance data was not fetched in the worktree so the rdf-tests suite could not be re-run here — FOLLOW-UP: run scripts/fetch-conformance.sh + sparq-conformance to confirm no regression in the fn-* string-function suite.

This bead is the audit record; the fix is on branch test-builtin-errors awaiting orchestrator merge.

title: N-Triples loader rejects RDF 1.2 triple-term <<( s p o )>> syntax (write/read asymmetry)
description: sparq-core's fast hand-written N-Triples parser (crates/sparq-core/src/nt.rs parse_chunk / parse_ntriples_parallel) does NOT recognise the N-Triples 1.2 triple-term object syntax <<( s p o )>>. ASYMMETRY: the engine STORES triple terms (Term::Triple), the Turtle loader PARSES <<( )>> fine, and sparq-engine's CONSTRUCT N-Triples serializer (construct::triples_to_ntriples) EMITS <<( )>> via oxrdf Display — but feeding that output back through Graph::load_str(.., "ntriples") fails with 'N-Triples: expected term start' at the <<( . So a CONSTRUCT->serialise->reload round-trip of a graph containing reified statements is lossy for N-Triples (works for Turtle). Repro: load ':r1 rdf:reifies <<( :a :age 30 )>> .' as turtle, construct_ntriples(CONSTRUCT {?s ?p ?o} WHERE {?s ?p ?o}), then Graph::load_str(out, "ntriples") -> Err. FIX: teach nt::parse_chunk (and parse_ntriples_parallel) to parse <<( s p o )>> in object position (N-Triples 1.2 / RDF-star); object-only, may nest. Until fixed, the rdf-star write coverage test crates/sparq-engine/tests/rdfstar_write.rs::ntriples_triple_term_reparse_is_a_known_gap is #[ignore]d and documents the desired behaviour. Found by sq-t267 (Opus 4.8).

title: MPC: semi-honest Shamir has NO tampered-share detection (malicious security gap, guarantee (D))
description: Pinned by sq-nuok adversarial suite (crates/sparq-mpc/src/adversarial_tests.rs, mod tamper). The honest-majority Shamir backend (shamir.rs reconstruct_at_zero / run_secure) performs plain Lagrange interpolation with NO consistency/integrity check. A single corrupted share silently changes the reconstructed secret with no error or signal — even when MAXIMAL redundancy is present (all n shares, of which any t+1 suffice): the impl does not cross-check subsets, so it neither detects nor corrects the inconsistent point. The same holds inside the secure-equality primitive: tampering one share of the opened product m=d·r flips a true MATCH into a non-match (or vice versa) undetected, and inside run_secure's summed sharing (corrupted aggregate). This is CORRECT for the stated semi-honest / honest-but-curious model — malicious security (guarantee (D), active deviation) is explicitly deferred (shamir.rs 'Security model'; backend.rs 'how the trust model stays CONFIGURABLE'). This bead is the durable record of the gap, NOT a request to implement it now. Remediation when malicious-honest-majority is scheduled: verifiable secret sharing (VSS) or information-theoretic MACs behind the SAME MpcBackend trait, reporting malicious_secure=true via BackendInfo. Tests already pin the current (undetected) behaviour so a future fix is observable: the assert_ne! tamper tests would need to become assert(detected-and-errors). NOTE: structural mismatches (wrong evaluation point in a linear op) ARE caught today as a typed Protocol error — only VALUE integrity is unchecked.

title: update_in_place is non-atomic on multi-op request failure (no engine-level rollback)
description: FINDING (sq-qu8o, contract tests in crates/sparq-engine/src/update.rs mod update_contract): a SPARQL UPDATE *request* is a ;-separated op sequence and per SPARQL 1.1 should be all-or-nothing, but the engine's delta-overlay entry point update_in_place(&mut Graph, sparql) applies ops in place and, on op K failing, leaves ops 0..K-1 committed (a partial prefix) — verified by test in_place_request_is_partial_on_error_by_contract. This is currently DOCUMENTED-and-relied-upon (sparq_serve::ApplyUpdates::apply contract; the serve writer recovers atomicity via fork -> apply -> seal-only-on-Ok), so the PRODUCTION HTTP path IS request-atomic. The rebuild path update() is atomic by construction (rebuild_request_is_atomic). The gap: any direct library consumer of update_in_place gets silent partial application on error — a footgun. Options: (a) add an atomic update_in_place wrapper (fork+seal internally) as the public default; (b) document the non-atomicity on update_in_place's rustdoc + steer callers to update() or the fork pattern; (c) leave as-is (serve is the only first-party caller). Low priority: no production-path bug, fully test-pinned. NOT a SILENT-contract bug — CLEAR/DROP/CREATE auto-create no-op success is spec-conformant (SHOULD, not MUST, conditioned on recording empty graphs).

title: Core: cheap O(overlay) Graph::snapshot API (Arc-shared immutable base)
description: Add a cheap Graph snapshot that shares the immutable base (perms + compacted dict arena) behind Arcs so snapshots are O(overlay), not O(triples). Unblocks the server double-buffer collapse, Python Graph.copy(), and the RSP overlay-snapshot EvalMode. Structural change across every storage mode (incl. mmap + compressed). Design in the design field. (was the workspace TODO.md cheap-snapshot rationale — now beaded + doc deleted)
design:
Cheap O(overlay) Graph snapshot API — the core structural change that unblocks the
server double-buffer collapse (sq-dfs), Python Graph.copy() (sq-6h8), and the RSP
overlay-snapshot EvalMode (sq-j39). (Design preserved from the deleted workspace TODO.md.)

PROBLEM. `Graph` is not (and should not be naively) `Clone`: a deep copy of the
dictionary arena and the six permutation indexes is O(n). The server's SPARQL Update
path (crates/sparq-server/src/http.rs::Writer) currently gets microsecond steady-state
updates WITHOUT core changes by double-buffering — two physical Graphs alternate between
*published* and *spare* — but that pays ~2x graph residency, a one-time O(graph) rebuild
on the first update (and again after a failed update discards a buffer), and a
spare-reclaim wait/rebuild when a reader holds a snapshot past the query budget.

PROPOSED API.
  - `Graph::snapshot(&self) -> GraphSnapshot` (or make `Graph` a cheap `Clone`): an O(1)
    copy that SHARES the immutable base — `TripleStore::perms` and the compacted dictionary
    storage behind `Arc`s — with the mutable parts (the delta `Overlay`, the append-only
    dictionary tail, the numeric-cache tail) either cloned (small, O(pending updates)) or
    made copy-on-write.
  - The server then keeps ONE master `Graph`, `update_in_place`s it (µs), and publishes
    `Arc::new(master.snapshot())` per commit. The publish slot stays
    `RwLock<Arc<Graph>>` + single-writer mutex; only the Writer's buffer juggling collapses.

REQUIREMENTS the API must meet:
  1. Snapshots are O(overlay), NEVER O(triples).
  2. Immutable and `Send + Sync`.
  3. Unaffected by later `update_in_place`/`compact` on the master — compaction must not
     invalidate live snapshots (the new base goes into FRESH `Arc`s).

COST / why it is structural (not an additive seam): meeting (1)–(3) means moving
`TripleStore`'s permutation storage and the dictionary's compacted arena behind `Arc`s — a
change to EVERY storage mode, including mmap + compressed. This is why sq-dfs / sq-6h8 /
sq-j39 are all blocked on it.

WINS over the current server double-buffer: removes the ~2x graph residency; removes the
one-time O(graph) rebuild the first update pays to materialise the second buffer (and the
re-pay after a failed update); removes the spare-reclaim wait/rebuild fallback when a
reader holds a snapshot past the query budget.
